newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches supplies for orbiting Mir station.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches supplies for orbiting Mir station.

text.p: Russia launched a supply rocket to its Mir orbiting space station on Wednesday, less than a week after the embarrassing failure of a $300 million mission to Mars.

A spokeswoman at the Russian space mission control said the supply satellite, launched aboard a Soyuz-U rocket from Kazakhstan's Baikonur cosmodrome, had reached its orbit. It was due to dock with Mir at 4 a.m. Moscow time (0100 GMT) on Friday.
The supply mission had been delayed for more than a month, mainly due to financial problems which postponed production of the booster rockets needed to send the supplies into orbit.
It is bringing scientific equipment, fuel, oxygen, water, food and instruments for Mir's crew of two Russians and American astronaut John Blaha, who have been aboard Mir since September.

The three, whose toilet tanks are almost overflowing, have already had their stay in space extended by some two months after cash problems forced the postponement of the launch of the next crew, which will include a German.
Four Mir launches have been held up this year because of a cash crunch in the Russian space industry.
The Russian space sector is still smarting from the loss of its Mars-96 unmanned space probe, which crashed into the Pacific Ocean after a booster failed.
Ths Mars mission had also delayed by two years, also due to cash shortages.
The ageing Mir station, launched in 1976, is the cornerstone of Russia's space programme. Space officials plan to replace it with a new international station, to be called Alpha.
